ideas.title: Climb anything
ideas.goal: As Lumi the player jumps at any wall, trunk or rock, catches whatever edge the claws reach, shimmies along it and pulls up, to reach places nobody can (the cottage roof, the top of the big pine, the sea stack). Fun because the island becomes a climbing route you read with your own eyes, and a missed grab is a real fall.
ideas.idea: Edges come from the real meshes: a Mantle kernel casts a fan of rays from Lumi's claws into the Raycore BVH and finds lips (a steep face under a flat top). Holding is not a constraint that pins Lumi: Lumi is a PrintSim affine body, the claws are two frictional contacts with IPC against the wall mesh (so it can never pass into the wall), and it holds only while the contact force stays inside the Coulomb friction cone of that material: on wet rock or a glossy roof it slides off, on bark it holds. Catching an edge at speed swings the body as a real pendulum; a pull-up is a motor torque with Lumi's real mass. Done means live_motion shows no snaps or jitter on the ledge, measured.
ideas.form: a jump-in ability on PrintSim contact plus a GPU edge finder; a traced film of the first climb up the cottage to the chimney, one slip on the wet gutter included

ideas.title: The bees and the smoker
ideas.goal: A swarm boils out of the hive and harasses the friends across the meadow; the player runs with a smoker and herds the swarm back home with smoke, like a twin stick game where your shot is a cloud. Fun because the swarm is alive and the smoke drifts with the wind, so you have to lead it.
ideas.idea: Smoke and the hive's scent are two fields on a GPU grid fluid on Mantle (advection, diffusion, buoyancy for the warm smoke, the island's wind at the boundary). The bees are a few hundred bodies with real insect flight on the GPU: thrust and drag give a 7 m/s cruise, wings beat at 230 Hz so the tracer's shutter blurs them into a disc like a real photo of a bee, they flee smoke concentration, climb the scent gradient where smoke is thick (smoked bees go home, as beekeepers rely on), and chase moving warm bodies otherwise. Each bee is a generated bee mesh, striped and furry, big enough to read at 2 m. Measured: swarm speed, fraction home over time, ms per frame.
ideas.form: a mini game on a GPU smoke solver and a swarm; a traced film at bee height of the smoke wall rolling the swarm into the hive

ideas.title: A rope bridge you tie yourself
ideas.goal: The player ties a rope between two trees or across the stream, knots planks onto it and walks across, and the bridge sags, sways and swings under every step, more the looser they tied it; friends cross it too, and a heavy friend on a badly tied bridge tips everyone into the water. Fun because the quality of what you build is what you feel when you walk it.
ideas.idea: The ropes are rod chains and the planks rigid bodies in PrintSim on the GPU (joints for the knots, IPC contact between planks and feet), with real tension so the sag follows a catenary and each step sends a wave along the bridge. The player chooses where the ends are tied and how tight; walking reads the plank under the foot each frame. A knot under too much tension slips.
ideas.form: a building tool in jump-in plus PrintSim ropes; a traced film of Lumi wobbling across while the pig waits its turn

ideas.title: The island floods at spring tide
ideas.goal: Once a month the spring tide comes up over the low meadow; the player races to move the friends' things to high ground, builds a dam of sods, and paddles a tub across the flooded garden. Fun as a short dramatic event with real choices about what to save and where the water will go.
ideas.idea: The water is a shallow-water solver on a GPU grid over the real terrain (Saint-Venant equations, wetting and drying), driven by the tide level from the moon's phase; it runs into the low ground through the actual gaps. Things float by their density (buoyancy on PrintSim bodies), sods add terrain height where the player lays them. The water stays a few hours, then drains back leaving wet dark ground.
ideas.form: a monthly event with a player role; a traced film of the tide spilling over the dune into the garden and the tub drifting
